caption: FT8 runs on a strict clock: stations take turns in 15-second transmit/receive slots, kept in lock-step by internet-synced computer clocks — and the mode decodes signals buried below the noise.
spoken: A timeline of two FT8 stations taking turns: each transmits for 15 seconds while the other listens, then they swap. Every computer's clock is synchronized, so the slots line up, and a whole contact fits in about a minute.
